rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only baseline has useful predictive signal. config_001 tests the simplest RNA setting (single profile, PCA n2000) without learned encoders, aggregation, or fusion. This is the best next experiment because it is low-cost, establishes a reference performance, and isolates the RNA representation before adding image, multiprofile aggregation, or multimodal fusion.

The only completed experiment is an RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline with modest validation accuracy, so it is still unclear whether the image modality carries useful signal. config_010 tests an image-only single-profile ResNet50 model, keeping the profile setting simple and avoiding aggregation or fusion changes, to establish a clean image baseline. This is the best next use of a limited experiment because it reduces uncertainty about a core design choice—whether image features are informative—before investing in multimodal, multiprofile, or more complex fusion settings.

The only strong result so far is RNA-only single-profile PCA (config_001), while image-only ResNet is weak. The key uncertainty is whether using multiple profiles improves the RNA representation. config_002 extends the best-known RNA baseline by adding multiprofile with a simple avgpool aggregation, avoiding simultaneous changes to RNA encoder, image modality, or fusion. It directly tests whether profile aggregation adds value before investing in more complex RNA encoders or multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool aggregation substantially outperforms singleprofile RNA, suggesting profile aggregation is important. The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve further over avgpool. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the best RNA setting fixed, so it cleanly tests aggregation quality. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising direction while isolating one important design choice before moving to more complex multimodal configurations.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool using PCA (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), which clearly outperforms single-profile RNA and image-only models, while transformer aggregation is weaker than avgpool. The main remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation improves over PCA under this promising profile/aggregation setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, cleanly isolating the representation effect. This is the best next use of budget because it tests the most important untested RNA design choice before adding multimodal complexity, and it will clarify whether learned RNA encoders should be pursued further.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile models with avgpool are promising, especially config_005 with scvi_n200 at 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1, while image-only and transformer-aggregation variants are weaker. The main remaining uncertainty is whether the current best performance is specific to scvi_n200 or whether another RNA representation, scgpt, can improve further under the same multiprofile avgpool setting. config_008 tests this by changing only the RNA encoder relative to the current best RNA configuration, isolating the effect of representation. It is the best next experiment because it either identifies a stronger encoder or confirms scvi_n200 as the preferred representation before adding more complexity such as fusion.

The strongest completed result is config_005, RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool, achieving 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1. Avgpool also outperformed transformer for pca_n2000 (0.591 vs 0.519), but it is unclear whether the better scvi representation changes the optimal aggregation. config_006 tests this directly by changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the best encoder and profile setting. This is a clean exploitation of the most promising direction and will clarify whether transformer aggregation is worth its added complexity before moving to multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models are strong, especially scvi_n200, but image-only evidence is sparse and poor: resnet50 singleprofile has accuracy 0.208. It is unclear whether image features are uninformative or whether singleprofile/no aggregation is the bottleneck. config_011 tests the same resnet50 image encoder with multiprofile avgpool, the profile/aggregation setting that improved RNA-only PCA from 0.485 to 0.591, thereby isolating the effect of profile/aggregation for image. This is a simpler, high-information experiment than moving directly to multimodal fusion or changing the image encoder, and it clarifies whether resnet image profiles are worth including in later multimodal comparisons.

RNA with scvi_n200 is the strongest direction so far, with multiprofile avgpool/transformer reaching about 0.65 accuracy and 0.63 F1, but single-profile scvi is untested. Multiprofile helped PCA and ResNet image baselines, yet we should not assume it is necessary for scvi. This experiment tests whether a simpler single-profile scvi model can match the multiprofile scvi results, clarifying the importance of profile/aggregation for the best RNA encoder. It is a high-value next step because it extends the most promising unimodal model, has high expected accuracy, and reduces uncertainty before adding multimodal fusion complexity.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool is currently the strongest direction (accuracy 0.650, F1 0.628), while image-only ResNet is weak (0.328 with multiprofile avgpool), leaving uncertainty about whether image information is complementary when fused with RNA. config_030 keeps the best RNA representation, profile setting, and aggregation, and adds only ResNet image features with simple concat fusion, directly testing whether multimodal fusion improves over the strong RNA baseline. This is a clean, minimal extension of the most promising evidence before testing more complex fusion, aggregation, or image-encoder choices.
